_comment: Reasoned statuses for failure-matrix cases that cannot be executed as live or automated tests yet. Used by scripts/matrix-coverage.py only when no test/lab evidence exists. 'blocked', 'partial' and 'not_applicable' are never counted as passed; 'verified_check' records an executed check script (exact command, artifacts and result) that CI re-runs on every release artifact.

TRUST-012.reason: Anvil does not ingest or correlate gateway logs; it never confirms anything from temporal proximity. Operator logs are used only as lab ground truth.

LOAD-012.reason: The optional JMeter adapter is not built in this release (plan 14.3: only after native load works). Native load covers the required workloads; see docs/load.md.

PROTO-004.reason: HTTP/2 GOAWAY and REFUSED_STREAM are typed (exchange.h2_goaway / exchange.h2_refused_stream, dispatch derived from REFUSED_STREAM) but a live multi-stream graceful-shutdown fixture is not built yet.

REL-001.reason: Hosted release smoke (.github/workflows/release-smoke.yml) against the published, unsigned anvil-v0.1.5 assets (each checked against SHA256SUMS): run 41189324002 on PR head adb4d3f, the same per-target result as the earlier run 41185287833 on head 7f17212. This evidence comes from pull_request-triggered runs against the published assets; once the workflow is on main, the run that publishing a release starts (release: published) is the routine check. For each target, the smoke installs the package natively on a fresh runner and launches the installed app (window and webview process observed). It then imports samples/workspaces/anvil-samples.anvil, sends its Healthy/OK request to a loopback listener (HTTP 200) and relaunches the app; a target stops at its first failed step. Six targets pass every step: macOS arm64 DMG (macos-15), macOS x86_64 DMG (native Intel macos-15-intel), Windows x64 NSIS and MSI (windows-2025), Linux x64 .deb (Ubuntu 26.04) and .rpm (Fedora 44). The x64 AppImage fails at its first launch (a package failure): the app starts and shows its window, but its WebKit web process aborts with EGL_BAD_PARAMETER, so it never reached the import, the call or the relaunch. An AppImage fix is in progress. The GUI was not driven: the import and the call go through the release CLI archive on the app's data directory. Recorded bypasses: Gatekeeper and SmartScreen were never consulted (the assets carried no quarantine attribute or Mark-of-the-Web); the DMG license was accepted non-interactively; the installers ran silently, the MSI as an administrator without a UAC prompt; local .deb/.rpm packages and the AppImage ran without a package-signature check. Still blocked: signed and notarized first-run acceptance on macOS and Windows (Gatekeeper, SmartScreen, Keychain), which needs owner credentials (ferrum-edge/ferrum-anvil#2). Linux has no platform code signing, so it waits on no credentials.

REL-003.reason: Only the valid path is executed: on macOS arm64 a signed in-app update installed and relaunched Anvil from 0.1.0 to 0.1.1. The refusal scenario (an invalidly signed or altered update refused without mutation) has not been executed. Release runs 36827029766 and 36835226571 produced the update; latest.json signatures verify against updater key BFE08514FEC0E65A. Windows and Linux were not exercised. macOS may re-prompt for Keychain access after an update, especially with unsigned builds; see ferrum-edge/ferrum-anvil#2 for Developer ID signing.

REL-006.reason: Checked by the website repository's tests at ferrum-edge/ferrumedge commit e4fe8b9a1b1de6b8dfeb021111bea262828fe57c (main after ferrum-edge/ferrumedge#105); its Test run 41182180521 (`node --test "tests/**/*.test.js"`) passed 403 of 405 tests, with the 2 live asset checks skipped. tests/fixtures/release-audit.json records the anvil-v0.1.5 audit: the 35 published assets with their GitHub SHA-256 digests, the published SHA256SUMS lines and the release-evidence.json targets. tests/anvil.test.js ('Anvil downloads match the release evidence') ties each download.html row's OS and architecture, and each link's package label and column, to the linked asset name (architecture aliases mapped; swapped architecture, OS, package or column rejected); requires every displayed download to be that platform's installer or CLI archive in release-evidence.json, and the table to show each of them once; checks that the recorded SHA256SUMS lines hash to GitHub's digest of the published SHA256SUMS asset, and that each of the 33 assets it lists has a recorded digest equal to its SHA256SUMS entry (only SHA256SUMS and release-evidence.json are unlisted). The digests are compared as recorded in the fixture, not re-downloaded on each run. The site displays no hashes and points to SHA256SUMS. Partial until Anvil's own CI re-runs these tests at that pinned commit on every release (.github/workflows/website-evidence.yml, called from release.yml) and a hosted run passes.

REL-007.reason: Checked by the website repository's tests at ferrum-edge/ferrumedge commit e4fe8b9a1b1de6b8dfeb021111bea262828fe57c (main after ferrum-edge/ferrumedge#105); its Test run 41182180521 (`node --test "tests/**/*.test.js"`) passed 403 of 405 tests, with the 2 live asset checks skipped. tests/components.test.js ('Anvil navigation entries') renders the shared nav and footer for root, nested (guides/, install/, plugins/) and extensionless or .html page paths and checks that the desktop Tools dropdown, the mobile menu and the footer link to Anvil as an unsigned preview with an extensionless link that resolves to /anvil from each page; that on the Anvil page Tools is active and the desktop and mobile Anvil links carry aria-current="page" (an Anvil guide activates Docs instead, and other Tools pages mark no Anvil link current); that no injected link uses .html; and that the dropdown toggles carry aria-controls. tests/anvil.test.js checks that local links in Anvil content are extensionless and resolve with their anchors, and that screenshots and brand images have alt text. This is targeted accessibility coverage (aria-current, aria-controls, alt text), not a full accessibility audit. Partial until Anvil's own CI re-runs these tests at that pinned commit on every release (.github/workflows/website-evidence.yml, called from release.yml) and a hosted run passes.

REL-008.reason: Checked by the website repository's tests at ferrum-edge/ferrumedge commit e4fe8b9a1b1de6b8dfeb021111bea262828fe57c (main after ferrum-edge/ferrumedge#105); its Test run 41182180521 (`node --test "tests/**/*.test.js"`) passed 403 of 405 tests, with the 2 live asset checks skipped. tests/anvil.test.js checks capability and limitation truth: no Anvil content (Anvil pages and the marked Anvil blocks on shared pages) claims an exact or guaranteed root cause or 'available now'; each carries the unsigned-preview notice naming v0.1.5; downloads distinguish installer code signing from updater signatures and point to SHA256SUMS; anvil.html names the eight supported Ferrum Edge catalog releases and the fallback for others in its compatibility and limitations sections; the support matrix lists gRPC over HTTP/3, gRPC-Web, SSE over HTTP/3, CONNECT-UDP, PROXY protocol, HBONE and 0-RTT early data, gives WebSocket, gRPC, gRPC-Web, SSE, TCP and UDP/DTLS a load unit, and its 'Not implemented' note lists the remaining gaps but no implemented protocol; and screenshots carry descriptive alt text and a 'Pre-release build' caption. Partial until Anvil's own CI re-runs these tests at that pinned commit on every release (.github/workflows/website-evidence.yml, called from release.yml) and a hosted run passes.

REL-002.reason: 2026-09-25, macOS arm64, commit cf3a61c: `npx tauri build --ci --bundles app,dmg` and `cargo build --release --locked -p anvil-cli`, then `scripts/release-check.sh --runtime-probe --probe-seconds 15` over the .app, the .dmg, the raw anvil-desktop binary and the anvil CLI → pass (graph: no tauri-plugin-wdio-webdriver / e2e feature; 0 of 11 hook strings; runtime probe: no WebDriver listener on TAURI_WEBDRIVER_PORT, no env-driven profile unlock). Negative control: the e2e debug build fails with all 11 strings. The release workflow runs the same check on every installer and archive.

UP-017.reason: Live reproduction blocked: Ferrum Edge 0.9.5 assigns port_exhaustion only to EADDRNOTAVAIL at connect (src/retry.rs) and the release binary has no lab dial-admission hook, while draining the lab host's real ephemeral ports would be unsafe. Covered instead by the public-signal contract test up_017_port_exhaustion_signal_is_coarse_and_hook_free (crates/anvil-diagnostics/tests/upstream_setup_contract.rs): the catalog's shared 502 connection_failure 'Backend unavailable' signal keeps the connection-failure family ambiguous, names port exhaustion only as an unknown-confidence candidate, never states port exhaustion or host resources at likely or above, and makes no TLS/DNS claim. It is neither a live nor a hook-based test.

UP-019.reason: Live reproduction blocked: upstream.trust_withdrawn is mesh-only in 0.9.5 and 0.9.7 (an accepted gateway trust publication withdraws an authority while an HBONE / sidecar-mTLS transport is established or reused). The mesh lab profile runs HBONE with SPIFFE identities and reproduces the unauthenticated-peer refusal, but it has no control plane publishing trust, so no withdrawal on a live tunnel is reproduced. Covered instead by the public-signal contract test up_019_trust_withdrawn_signal_makes_no_certificate_claim (crates/anvil-diagnostics/tests/upstream_setup_contract.rs): the shared 502 connection_failure signal stays ambiguous, lists trust withdrawal only as an unknown-confidence candidate, and yields no confirmed or likely certificate/TLS claim and no blame on the caller's certificate.
